sections.title: Quick reactions in conversation: meaning and form
body: Goal: Respond naturally to good news, bad news, suggestions and misunderstandings, then add a relevant follow-up.
Core vocabulary: en reaktion, förvånad, beklagar. Key phrases: Vad roligt! Berätta mer. · Vad tråkigt. Hur mår du nu? · Det låter bra, men vilken tid passar?

A useful reaction has two parts: acknowledge what you heard and continue the exchange. Choose a reaction that matches the situation: Vad roligt!, Vad tråkigt!, Det låter bra, Jag förstår or Ursäkta, hur menar du? Avoid using jaha alone when warmth or clarity matters.
Say the examples aloud, notice the pattern, and then change one detail rather than memorising a fixed script.

body: Register model: “Vad tråkigt att höra.” is a warm neutral response way to express “I am sorry to hear that.”.
For listening and reading, answer from a specific word or phrase. For speaking and writing, make the recipient, purpose and next action clear.
Attempt the task before using the model. Improve one high-impact feature, then perform it again with the transfer condition.

assignment.title: Four-skill task and transfer
assignment.instructions:
LISTEN: First listen without a transcript. Answer: Which reaction best fits? Replay once and identify the exact words that prove the answer.

READ: Read for purpose and evidence. Answer: Which response best acknowledges Jo's situation? Mark the shortest phrase that supports your choice.

SPEAK: Respond to four short prompts: good news, illness, a practical suggestion and an unclear instruction. Add one useful follow-up each time. Make a first attempt, check clarity and repeat once.

WRITE: Write three brief message replies that show warmth and move the situation forward: congratulations, sympathy and a changed plan. Check reader, purpose, required details and next action.

TRANSFER: You are speaking to a colleague rather than a close friend; keep the reaction warm but use neutral workplace language.

BETWEEN LESSON · Optional, 5 minutes: retrieve the three key phrases without looking, then use one in a new sentence.
